import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.14

by O. H. Kegel

b) Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes
$L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of,
respectively, all locally nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups,
all locally soluble torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups.
Is it true that $G$ is characteristically simple?

The notebook remarks that the existential closedness of $G$ is a local property, so it seems
difficult to obtain global properties of $G$ from it. Part a) of the problem is solved and has
been moved to the Archive of the notebook; it is not stated here.

A group $G$ is *existentially closed* in a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups if $G \in \mathfrak{X}$
and every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in $G$ that has a solution
in some group $H \in \mathfrak{X}$ containing $G$ as a subgroup already has a solution in $G$.
A group is *locally nilpotent* (resp. *locally soluble*) if all its finitely generated subgroups
are nilpotent (resp. soluble). It is *torsion-free* if $1$ is its only element of finite order.
For a set of primes $\pi$, it is a *$\pi$-group* if every element has finite order all of whose
prime divisors lie in $\pi$. A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic
subgroups are the trivial subgroup and the whole group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
universe u
namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

structure EqSystem (G : Type u) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The words `w` standing for the equations `w = 1`. -/
  eqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))
  /-- The words `w` standing for the inequations `w ≠ 1`. -/
  neqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))
blocks.docstring:
A finite system of equations and inequations over the group `G` in `n` unknowns. Words are
elements of the free group on the alphabet `G ⊕ Fin n`: letters from `G` are the coefficients and
letters from `Fin n` are the unknowns. A word `w ∈ eqs` stands for the equation `w = 1` and a word
`w ∈ neqs` stands for the inequation `w ≠ 1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Monoid.Coprod / Monoid.CoprodI (free products) and FirstOrder.Language formulas (Mathlib has a ring language but no group language); FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n) with FreeGroup.lift gives the same expressive power far more simply.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.14».EqSystem
justification.why_needed: A finite system of equations and inequations over a group G in n unknowns: two Finsets of words in FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n) (letters from G are coefficients, letters from Fin n are unknowns); w ∈ eqs means w = 1, w ∈ neqs means w ≠ 1. Mathlib has no notion of equations over a group with coefficients.

blocks.name: EqSystem
blocks.text:
/-- A finite system of equations and inequations over the group `G` in `n` unknowns. Words are
elements of the free group on the alphabet `G ⊕ Fin n`: letters from `G` are the coefficients and
letters from `Fin n` are the unknowns. A word `w ∈ eqs` stands for the equation `w = 1` and a word
`w ∈ neqs` stands for the inequation `w ≠ 1`. -/
structure EqSystem (G : Type u) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The words `w` standing for the equations `w = 1`. -/
  eqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))
  /-- The words `w` standing for the inequations `w ≠ 1`. -/
  neqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))

blocks.code:
def EqSystem.IsSolution {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] {n : ℕ} (S : EqSystem G n)
    (f : G →* H) (v : Fin n → H) : Prop :=
  (∀ w ∈ S.eqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w = 1) ∧
    (∀ w ∈ S.neqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w ≠ 1)
blocks.docstring:
The assignment `v` of the unknowns is a solution in the group `H` of the system `S` over `G`,
where the coefficients from `G` are interpreted in `H` via the homomorphism `f`: every word of
`S.eqs` evaluates to `1` and no word of `S.neqs` evaluates to `1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift (used inside); no existing 'solution of a system' predicate.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.14».EqSystem.IsSolution
justification.why_needed: Evaluates a system in a group H via a hom f : G →* H on coefficients and an assignment v : Fin n → H on unknowns, using FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v); every eqs word evaluates to 1 and no neqs word does.

blocks.name: EqSystem.IsSolution
blocks.text:
/-- The assignment `v` of the unknowns is a solution in the group `H` of the system `S` over `G`,
where the coefficients from `G` are interpreted in `H` via the homomorphism `f`: every word of
`S.eqs` evaluates to `1` and no word of `S.neqs` evaluates to `1`. -/
def EqSystem.IsSolution {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] {n : ℕ} (S : EqSystem G n)
    (f : G →* H) (v : Fin n → H) : Prop :=
  (∀ w ∈ S.eqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w = 1) ∧
    (∀ w ∈ S.neqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w ≠ 1)

def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop) (G : Type u) [Group G] :
    Prop :=
  𝒳 G ∧ ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝒳 H → ∀ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : EqSystem G n), (∃ v : Fin n → H, S.IsSolution f v) →
      ∃ v : Fin n → G, S.IsSolution (MonoidHom.id G) v
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is *existentially closed* in the class `𝒳` of groups if `G` belongs to `𝒳`
and, for every group `H` in `𝒳` containing `G` as a subgroup (i.e. with an injective
homomorphism `G →* H`), every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in
`G` that has a solution in `H` already has a solution in `G`.

The group `H` ranges over the same universe as `G`. This is harmless for classes of groups that
are closed under subgroups and isomorphisms, such as the four classes of Problem 8.14: a solution
in `H` lies in the subgroup generated by the image of `G` and the solution.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib ModelTheory for IsExistentiallyClosed / existentially closed — nothing exists.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.14».IsExistentiallyClosedIn
justification.why_needed: G is existentially closed in the class 𝒳 (𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop): 𝒳 G and for every H with 𝒳 H and injective f : G →* H, every finite system of equations and inequations over G solvable in H is solvable in G. Mathlib has no notion of existential closedness (neither model-theoretic nor algebraic).

blocks.name: IsExistentiallyClosedIn
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` is *existentially closed* in the class `𝒳` of groups if `G` belongs to `𝒳`
and, for every group `H` in `𝒳` containing `G` as a subgroup (i.e. with an injective
homomorphism `G →* H`), every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in
`G` that has a solution in `H` already has a solution in `G`.

The group `H` ranges over the same universe as `G`. This is harmless for classes of groups that
are closed under subgroups and isomorphisms, such as the four classes of Problem 8.14: a solution
in `H` lies in the subgroup generated by the image of `G` and the solution. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop) (G : Type u) [Group G] :
    Prop :=
  𝒳 G ∧ ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝒳 H → ∀ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : EqSystem G n), (∃ v : Fin n → H, S.IsSolution f v) →
      ∃ v : Fin n → G, S.IsSolution (MonoidHom.id G) v

def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

This is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injectivity of `x ↦ x ^ n` for `n ≠ 0`), which
for non-abelian groups additionally demands uniqueness of roots.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsMulTorsionFree (rejected as too strong for non-abelian groups; isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder requires CommGroup), Monoid.IsTorsion (the opposite notion).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.14».IsTorsionFreeGroup
justification.why_needed: ∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1. Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree means x ↦ x^n is injective for n ≠ 0, which for non-abelian groups is strictly stronger (unique roots; e.g. the Klein bottle group ⟨a,b | a²=b²⟩ is torsion-free and soluble but not IsMulTorsionFree), so it would misformalize the classes L𝔑⁺ and especially L𝔖⁺. The former Monoid.IsTorsionFree no longer exists in Mathlib.

blocks.name: IsTorsionFreeGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

This is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injectivity of `x ↦ x ^ n` for `n ≠ 0`), which
for non-abelian groups additionally demands uniqueness of roots. -/
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π
blocks.docstring:
For a set of primes `π`, a group `G` is a *`π`-group* if every element of `G` has finite order
and every prime divisor of the order of every element of `G` lies in `π`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsPGroup p G (single prime; a π-group is not a conjunction/disjunction of these).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.14».IsPiGroup
justification.why_needed: For π : Set Nat.Primes, every element has finite order and every prime dividing orderOf g lies in π. Mathlib only has IsPGroup for a single prime.

blocks.name: IsPiGroup
blocks.text:
/-- For a set of primes `π`, a group `G` is a *`π`-group* if every element of `G` has finite order
and every prime divisor of the order of every element of `G` lies in `π`. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π

def IsCharacteristicallySimple (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤
blocks.docstring:
A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup `⊥` and the whole group `⊤`. With this convention the trivial group is
characteristically simple.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsSimpleGroup (normal rather than characteristic subgroups, and requires Nontrivial).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.14».IsCharacteristicallySimple
justification.why_needed: ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤. Mathlib has Subgroup.Characteristic but no characteristic simplicity.

blocks.name: IsCharacteristicallySimple
blocks.text:
/-- A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup `⊥` and the whole group `⊤`. With this convention the trivial group is
characteristically simple. -/

  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isPiGroup_singleton_iff_isPGroup (p : Nat.Primes) :
    IsPiGroup {p} G ↔ IsPGroup p G := by
  haveI : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime := ⟨p.2⟩
  rw [IsPGroup.iff_orderOf]
  refine forall_congr' fun g => ⟨fun ⟨hg, hp⟩ => ?_, fun ⟨k, hk⟩ => ⟨?_, fun q hq => ?_⟩⟩
  · exact ⟨_, Nat.eq_prime_pow_of_unique_prime_dvd hg.orderOf_pos.ne' fun hq hd =>
      congrArg Subtype.val (hp ⟨_, hq⟩ hd)⟩
  · exact orderOf_pos_iff.mp (hk ▸ pow_pos p.2.pos k)
  · rw [hk] at hq
    exact Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr (Subtype.ext ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq q.2 p.2).mp
      (q.2.dvd_of_dvd_pow hq)))
blocks.docstring: A group is a `{p}`-group if and only if it is a `p`-group.
blocks.name: isPiGroup_singleton_iff_isPGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group is a `{p}`-group if and only if it is a `p`-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isPiGroup_singleton_iff_isPGroup (p : Nat.Primes) :
    IsPiGroup {p} G ↔ IsPGroup p G := by
  haveI : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime := ⟨p.2⟩
  rw [IsPGroup.iff_orderOf]
  refine forall_congr' fun g => ⟨fun ⟨hg, hp⟩ => ?_, fun ⟨k, hk⟩ => ⟨?_, fun q hq => ?_⟩⟩
  · exact ⟨_, Nat.eq_prime_pow_of_unique_prime_dvd hg.orderOf_pos.ne' fun hq hd =>
      congrArg Subtype.val (hp ⟨_, hq⟩ hd)⟩
  · exact orderOf_pos_iff.mp (hk ▸ pow_pos p.2.pos k)
  · rw [hk] at hq
    exact Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr (Subtype.ext ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq q.2 p.2).mp
      (q.2.dvd_of_dvd_pow hq)))

theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      (IsExistentiallyClosedIn
          (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallyNilpotent H ∧ IsTorsionFreeGroup H) G ∨
        (∃ π : Set Nat.Primes, π.Nonempty ∧
          IsExistentiallyClosedIn (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H ∧ IsPiGroup π H) G) ∨
        IsExistentiallyClosedIn
          (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H ∧ IsTorsionFreeGroup H) G ∨
        IsExistentiallyClosedIn (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H) G) →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$,
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of, respectively, all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups (for some set of primes $\pi$),
all locally soluble torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups. Is it true that $G$ is
characteristically simple?

The set of primes $\pi$ is required to be nonempty: for $\pi = \emptyset$ the class
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ consists of the trivial groups only, and the question would degenerate to
the convention on whether the trivial group is characteristically simple.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.14

by O. H. Kegel

b) Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes
$L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of,
respectively, all locally nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups,
all locally soluble torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups.
Is it true that $G$ is characteristically simple?

The notebook remarks that the existential closedness of $G$ is a local property, so it seems
difficult to obtain global properties of $G$ from it. Part a) of the problem is solved and has
been moved to the Archive of the notebook; it is not stated here.

A group $G$ is *existentially closed* in a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups if $G \in \mathfrak{X}$
and every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in $G$ that has a solution
in some group $H \in \mathfrak{X}$ containing $G$ as a subgroup already has a solution in $G$.
A group is *locally nilpotent* (resp. *locally soluble*) if all its finitely generated subgroups
are nilpotent (resp. soluble). It is *torsion-free* if $1$ is its only element of finite order.
For a set of primes $\pi$, it is a *$\pi$-group* if every element has finite order all of whose
prime divisors lie in $\pi$. A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic
subgroups are the trivial subgroup and the whole group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

/-- A finite system of equations and inequations over the group `G` in `n` unknowns. Words are
elements of the free group on the alphabet `G ⊕ Fin n`: letters from `G` are the coefficients and
letters from `Fin n` are the unknowns. A word `w ∈ eqs` stands for the equation `w = 1` and a word
`w ∈ neqs` stands for the inequation `w ≠ 1`. -/
structure EqSystem (G : Type u) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The words `w` standing for the equations `w = 1`. -/
  eqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))
  /-- The words `w` standing for the inequations `w ≠ 1`. -/
  neqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))

/-- The assignment `v` of the unknowns is a solution in the group `H` of the system `S` over `G`,
where the coefficients from `G` are interpreted in `H` via the homomorphism `f`: every word of
`S.eqs` evaluates to `1` and no word of `S.neqs` evaluates to `1`. -/
def EqSystem.IsSolution {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] {n : ℕ} (S : EqSystem G n)
    (f : G →* H) (v : Fin n → H) : Prop :=
  (∀ w ∈ S.eqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w = 1) ∧
    (∀ w ∈ S.neqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w ≠ 1)

/-- A group `G` is *existentially closed* in the class `𝒳` of groups if `G` belongs to `𝒳`
and, for every group `H` in `𝒳` containing `G` as a subgroup (i.e. with an injective
homomorphism `G →* H`), every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in
`G` that has a solution in `H` already has a solution in `G`.

The group `H` ranges over the same universe as `G`. This is harmless for classes of groups that
are closed under subgroups and isomorphisms, such as the four classes of Problem 8.14: a solution
in `H` lies in the subgroup generated by the image of `G` and the solution. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop) (G : Type u) [Group G] :
    Prop :=
  𝒳 G ∧ ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝒳 H → ∀ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : EqSystem G n), (∃ v : Fin n → H, S.IsSolution f v) →
      ∃ v : Fin n → G, S.IsSolution (MonoidHom.id G) v

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group is *locally soluble* (locally solvable) if every finitely generated subgroup is
soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

This is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injectivity of `x ↦ x ^ n` for `n ≠ 0`), which
for non-abelian groups additionally demands uniqueness of roots. -/
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- For a set of primes `π`, a group `G` is a *`π`-group* if every element of `G` has finite order
and every prime divisor of the order of every element of `G` lies in `π`. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π

/-- A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup `⊥` and the whole group `⊤`. With this convention the trivial group is
characteristically simple. -/
def IsCharacteristicallySimple (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

section API

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group existentially closed in a class of groups belongs to that class. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsExistentiallyClosedIn.mem {𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop} {G : Type u} [Group G]
    (h : IsExistentiallyClosedIn 𝒳 G) : 𝒳 G :=
  h.1

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A soluble group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable [IsSolvable G] : IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A group with unique roots is torsion-free. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsTorsionFreeGroup.of_isMulTorsionFree [IsMulTorsionFree G] : IsTorsionFreeGroup G :=
  fun _ hg => by_contra fun h => not_isOfFinOrder_of_isMulTorsionFree h hg

/-- A group is a `{p}`-group if and only if it is a `p`-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isPiGroup_singleton_iff_isPGroup (p : Nat.Primes) :
    IsPiGroup {p} G ↔ IsPGroup p G := by
  haveI : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime := ⟨p.2⟩
  rw [IsPGroup.iff_orderOf]
  refine forall_congr' fun g => ⟨fun ⟨hg, hp⟩ => ?_, fun ⟨k, hk⟩ => ⟨?_, fun q hq => ?_⟩⟩
  · exact ⟨_, Nat.eq_prime_pow_of_unique_prime_dvd hg.orderOf_pos.ne' fun hq hd =>
      congrArg Subtype.val (hp ⟨_, hq⟩ hd)⟩
  · exact orderOf_pos_iff.mp (hk ▸ pow_pos p.2.pos k)
  · rw [hk] at hq
    exact Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr (Subtype.ext ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq q.2 p.2).mp
      (q.2.dvd_of_dvd_pow hq)))

/-- A simple group is characteristically simple. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsCharacteristicallySimple.of_isSimpleGroup [IsSimpleGroup G] :
    IsCharacteristicallySimple G :=
  fun H _ => IsSimpleGroup.eq_bot_or_eq_top_of_normal H (Subgroup.normal_of_characteristic H)

/-- The trivial group is characteristically simple. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsCharacteristicallySimple.of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] :
    IsCharacteristicallySimple G :=
  fun H _ => Or.inl H.eq_bot_of_subsingleton

end API

/--
Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$,
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of, respectively, all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups (for some set of primes $\pi$),
all locally soluble torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups. Is it true that $G$ is
characteristically simple?

The set of primes $\pi$ is required to be nonempty: for $\pi = \emptyset$ the class
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ consists of the trivial groups only, and the question would degenerate to
the convention on whether the trivial group is characteristically simple.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      (IsExistentiallyClosedIn
          (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallyNilpotent H ∧ IsTorsionFreeGroup H) G ∨
        (∃ π : Set Nat.Primes, π.Nonempty ∧
          IsExistentiallyClosedIn (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H ∧ IsPiGroup π H) G) ∨
        IsExistentiallyClosedIn
          (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H ∧ IsTorsionFreeGroup H) G ∨
        IsExistentiallyClosedIn (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H) G) →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry

/--
Is every group that is existentially closed in the class $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$ of all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups characteristically simple?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b.variants.locally_nilpotent_torsion_free : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsExistentiallyClosedIn
        (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallyNilpotent H ∧ IsTorsionFreeGroup H) G →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry

/--
Let $\pi$ be a nonempty set of primes. Is every group that is existentially closed in the class
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ of all locally soluble $\pi$-groups characteristically simple?

The set of primes $\pi$ is required to be nonempty: for $\pi = \emptyset$ the class
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ consists of the trivial groups only, and the question would degenerate to
the convention on whether the trivial group is characteristically simple.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b.variants.locally_soluble_pi : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (π : Set Nat.Primes), π.Nonempty → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsExistentiallyClosedIn (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H ∧ IsPiGroup π H) G →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry

/--
Is every group that is existentially closed in the class $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$ of all locally
soluble torsion-free groups characteristically simple?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b.variants.locally_soluble_torsion_free : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsExistentiallyClosedIn
        (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H ∧ IsTorsionFreeGroup H) G →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry

/--
Is every group that is existentially closed in the class $L\mathfrak{S}$ of all locally soluble
groups characteristically simple?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b.variants.locally_soluble : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsExistentiallyClosedIn (fun H [Group H] => IsLocallySolvable H) G →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.14»

items: Existential closedness is formalized via finite systems of equations and inequations with coefficients in G (words in FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n)), which is equivalent to the model-theoretic formulation with existential formulas with parameters from G (DNF + distributing ∃ over ∨). Inequations are included, as in the standard notion of 'existentially closed' (as opposed to 'algebraically closed').

'G ≤ H' is modeled as an injective group homomorphism G →* H with H in the same universe as G (Type). This is harmless for all four classes: each is closed under subgroups, and a solution in a large H lives in the subgroup generated by the image of G and finitely many elements, which has small cardinality.
IsExistentiallyClosedIn includes the requirement G ∈ 𝒳, following the standard definition.
Torsion-free is defined as 'only the identity has finite order' (IsTorsionFreeGroup), deliberately NOT Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree, which for non-abelian groups is the stronger unique-roots property.

The set of primes π is taken as π : Set Nat.Primes and required to be nonempty. For π = ∅ the class L𝔖_π consists only of trivial groups, the trivial group is then existentially closed in it, and the answer would depend purely on the convention of whether the trivial group is characteristically simple; excluding this degenerate case is robust to either convention. For nonempty π (and for the other three classes) existentially closed groups are automatically nontrivial, so the chosen definition of IsCharacteristicallySimple (no Nontrivial requirement) agrees with the alternative convention on all groups the statement actually quantifies over.

The primary slot is stated with a disjunctive hypothesis ('existentially closed in one of the classes'), with π existentially quantified inside the disjunct; this is equivalent to the conjunction over the four classes with π universally quantified.
Locally nilpotent / locally soluble mean every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) is nilpotent / soluble.

Two short proved API lemmas were added for the bespoke definitions (an existentially closed group lies in its class; a simple group is characteristically simple), as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes:
Final file is c01's declarations essentially verbatim (dropped an unused [Group G] argument from the EqSystem structure, expanded the module docstring, added a remark on the universe of the overgroup H, and ported five short proved API/test lemmas from c02 to exercise the bespoke definitions: IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent, IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable, IsTorsionFreeGroup.of_isMulTorsionFree, isPiGroup_singleton_iff_isPGroup, IsCharacteristicallySimple.of_subsingleton). Compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.

Modeling points a human should know: (1) 'G ≤ H' is an injective hom G →* H with H in the same universe (Type); harmless since all four classes are subgroup- and isomorphism-closed. (2) Existential closedness includes G ∈ 𝔛 and uses finite systems of equations w = 1 and inequations w ≠ 1 with coefficients in G (words in FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n)); this is equivalent to the model-theoretic definition via DNF. (3) Torsion-free deliberately avoids Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (unique roots), which would change the class L𝔖⁺; candidates c04, c05, c06, c07 used IsMulTorsionFree and were therefore not used. (4) π ranges over Set Nat.Primes and is required nonempty; for π = ∅ the class L𝔖_π is the trivial groups only and the statement would hinge on whether the trivial group counts as characteristically simple, so the degenerate case is excluded and documented (the decomposition notes allow either this restriction or an explicit convention). (5) Characteristically simple = every Subgroup.Characteristic subgroup is ⊥ or ⊤; with the nonempty-π restriction, all groups quantified over are nontrivial, so the convention does not affect the truth value. (6) Theorem names follow the existing Kourovka files (namespace Kourovka.«8.14», theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b...). No candidate omitted any slot; all objections/decompositions agreed that only part b) is posed and the closing remark is commentary.
